---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Headings at the levels the filter gives them."
description: "Each offset attribute applied to a real heading, so the rendered level and the page contents show the result."
---

Every heading below carries the attribute shown above it, and the filter sets its level as this page is rendered.
The contents list beside the page reflects the levels after offsetting, not the ones written.

This page sets no document-level `by`, so each heading shows what its own attribute does.

## A heading with no offset

Written as `## A heading with no offset`, and rendered at level two.

## Pushed down one level {offset-headings-by="1"}

Written as `## Pushed down one level {offset-headings-by="1"}`, and rendered at level three.

### Carried along by the cascade

Written as `### Carried along by the cascade`, with no attribute of its own.
The cascade is on by default, so it moves with its parent and is rendered at level four.

## Cascade turned off {offset-headings-by="1" offset-headings-recursive="false"}

Written with `offset-headings-recursive="false"`, so the offset applies to this heading alone.

### Left where it was

No attribute, and no cascade reaching it, so this stays at level three.

## Capped before it gets there {offset-headings-by="3" offset-headings-max-level="4"}

Written as `{offset-headings-by="3" offset-headings-max-level="4"}`.

Two plus three is five, and the cap holds it at level four.

## Cascade with a depth limit {offset-headings-by="1" offset-headings-depth="1"}

Written as `{offset-headings-by="1" offset-headings-depth="1"}`.

### Within the limit

One level below the attributed heading, so it inherits the offset.

#### Beyond the limit

Two levels below, so the cascade does not reach it and it keeps its level.

## Pulled up a level {offset-headings-by="-1"}

Written as `## Pulled up a level {offset-headings-by="-1"}`, and rendered at level one.

A negative offset pulls a heading towards the top of the document.

## Held at level one {offset-headings-by="-3"}

Written as `## Held at level one {offset-headings-by="-3"}`.

Two minus three is minus one, and level one is the top of the range.
The heading stops there, and the filter stays silent, because the range one to six is a limit rather than a mistake.

## Held at level six {offset-headings-by="5"}

Written as `## Held at level six {offset-headings-by="5"}`.

Two plus five is seven, and level six is the bottom of the range.
The heading stops there, again with no message.

## Where a cascade stops {offset-headings-by="1"}

Written as `## Where a cascade stops {offset-headings-by="1"}`, with the cascade left on.

### Carried down with it

Written deeper than the heading above, so the cascade reaches it, and it is rendered at level four.

## Back outside the cascade

Written at level two, the same level as the attributed heading above.
A cascade stops at the first heading back at that level, so this one keeps level two.

## Shifting the whole document

Rather than annotating each heading, set one offset for all of them:

```yaml
extensions:
  offset-headings:
    by: 1
```

The two add together, so a heading attribute adjusts that figure rather than replacing it, and a `-1` attribute cancels it exactly.

## Setting the cascade defaults once

`recursive` and `depth` are document-level options as well, beside `by`:

```yaml
extensions:
  offset-headings:
    recursive: false
    depth: 1
```

Each one supplies the value a heading uses when it writes no attribute of its own.
With `recursive: false`, a heading marked `{offset-headings-by="1"}` moves on its own, and `offset-headings-recursive="true"` opts one heading back in.
With `depth: 1`, a cascade reaches one level below the heading that starts it, and `offset-headings-depth="0"` gives one heading an unlimited cascade again.

Neither option can be shown on this page.
A document-level option applies to every heading in its document, and one page cannot hold two settings at once.
See the [Reference](reference.qmd#document-options) for the full list.

## When the filter warns

Most corrections are silent.
The clamp to the range one to six is one of them, as the headings held at level one and at level six show.

The snippets below are quoted rather than rendered, so this page stays free of the messages they produce.

A value the schema does not accept is named once.
The heading then keeps the document offset alone, and it starts no cascade:

```markdown
## Section {offset-headings-by="1.5"}
```

```text
(W) [offset-headings] Header.offset-headings-by: must be of type "integer", got "string".
```

A `max-level` outside the range one to six is named twice.
The schema names the value, and the filter names the level it settles on:

```markdown
## Section {offset-headings-by="3" offset-headings-max-level="8"}
```

```text
(W) [offset-headings] Header.offset-headings-max-level: must be at most 6, got 8.
(W) [offset-headings] Clamping "offset-headings-max-level" value 8 to 6 (must be in the range [1, 6]).
```

The same pair follows the `max-level` document option, where the schema reports an error rather than a warning:

```text
(E) [offset-headings] max-level: must be at most 6, got 8.
(W) [offset-headings] Clamping "max-level" value 8 to 6 (must be in the range [1, 6]).
```

The render finishes in every case.
The [Reference](reference.qmd#validation) gives the rule behind each message.

## Quarto's automatic shift

The filter raises this warning for Typst output, and for PDF output with numbered sections, so an HTML page such as this one cannot show it.
A Typst document with no level-one heading produces it:

```markdown
---
title: "Report"
format: typst
filters:
  - offset-headings
---

## Section
```

```text
(W) [offset-headings] Quarto applies "shift-heading-level-by: -1" to this typst output after this filter runs, shifting every heading one level up, unless "shift-heading-level-by" is set explicitly. Set "shift-heading-level-by: 0" in the front matter to keep the levels this filter produces, then silence this warning with "quarto-shift-warning: false" under "extensions.offset-headings" (an explicit "shift-heading-level-by" is invisible to Lua filters).
```

`shift-heading-level-by: 0` stops the shift, and the warning still appears, because a Lua filter cannot see that the option is set.
Both lines are needed, one to keep the levels and one to quieten the filter:

```yaml
shift-heading-level-by: 0
extensions:
  offset-headings:
    quarto-shift-warning: false
```

The filter reads the heading levels as they are written, before any offset.
A document that writes one heading at level one therefore gets no warning at all.
The [Reference](reference.qmd#quartos-automatic-shift) gives the exact condition and explains why a filter cannot cancel the shift.
